Subject: MAP: cost assumptions & token/unit-econ sync for evaluation

Tom — thanks for the call today. Per our MAP milestone 2 (evaluation + cost signoff) I wanted to align on the concrete unit-economics assumptions we should bake into the pilot so your procurement and engineering teams can validate. Attached is our lightweight MAP_cost_template.xlsx to capture the numbers. Quick asks: 

- Can you confirm the typical request payload sizes (tokens in / out) for the 3 top call types you plan to exercise in the eval?
- Any expected distribution of interactive vs. batch inference? (e.g., 70% interactive web calls, 30% nightly bulk scoring)
- Do you have a preferred caching TTL for results that are idempotent (search/rerank) vs. generative summaries?

High level from our side we usually model three levers for MAP gating: tokens/request, effective batching factor (requests consolidated per GPU call), and cache hit rate (prefix+KV). If we can get traffic slices + a small sample of representative prompts we’ll populate the token model and return an ops-ready cost sensitivity (tokens/$) for the pilot.

Next steps: if you can drop the traffic CSV and a couple sample requests by EOD Friday we’ll turn around an initial tokens-per-dollar spreadsheet and a recommended evaluation runbook (canary of 10k requests/day, 3-day steady window).

Attachments: MAP_cost_template.xlsx (stub)

— Hannah
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 11:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MAP: cost assumptions & token/unit-econ sync for evaluation

Hannah — thanks, attached is the traffic profile and a short sample of prompts. A few clarifications from my side: 

- Typical token sizes: search queries ~30–80 tokens in, rerank context ~400–900 tokens in, summary/generation ~1,200–2,000 tokens in (we expect longer summaries for batch). Output tokens vary — average generation output ~300 tokens.
- Distribution: roughly 65% interactive (search + rerank), 35% batch (nightly summaries and aggregate scoring).
- For caching: we can tolerate a 10–15m TTL for rerank caches (prefix-based) and longer TTLs for exact-match search results, but summaries must be regenerated — no caching for generative outputs. Also we do request de-dup at the edge (app-level) so effective duplicate requests are low.

Attaching: MediQuery_Traffic_Profile.csv

Let us know if you need more granular histograms.

Thanks,
Tom
VP Product, MediQuery
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Feb 2028 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: cost assumptions & token/unit-econ sync for evaluation

Hannah / Ben — I reviewed Tom's traffic file and sketched a conservative tokens/$ model. Key proposed assumptions (for the MAP eval phase):

1) Tokens per request (we'll model three classes):
   - Search: 60 tokens in, 40 tokens out (effective 100 tokens per request)
   - Rerank: 700 tokens context, 8 tokens per candidate (avg 5 candidates evaluated) => ~740 in / 0 out (scores only) => model as 740 tokens per rerank call
   - Summaries (batch): 1,600 tokens in, 300 tokens out => 1,900 tokens per request

2) Batching: assume interactive path batching factor = 1.5 (small coalescing at 50ms), batch path = 8 (nightly jobs consolidate). These are conservative; we can run microbenchmarks during the canary to calibrate.

3) Caching: assume 25% cache hit rate for search (prefix exact matches) and 0% for summaries. Rerank caching: 10% hit rate for candidate reuse. We’ll parameterize these in the spreadsheet so procurement can stress different scenarios.

4) Evaluation plan: canary = 10k requests/day for 3 days (mixed distribution per Tom's profile), then 100k/day for 2 days if stable. We recommend measuring token consumption, 95th percentile latency, and model-quality delta vs baseline (we'll provide eval prompts in: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-eval-plan).

5) Financial modeling: initial estimate (mid scenario) -> 0.75M tokens/day => $X/day (placeholder) — I’ll populate the exact tokens/$ once we pick a pricing tier and quantization profile.

I quoted Tom's message below to keep context. If OK, I’ll push an updated MAP_cost_template.xlsx into the Drive and tag the HubSpot deal (HUBSPOT-34921).

Tom / Priya / Procurement — thanks for the quick turnaround and the profile. We've baked Aditya's assumptions into the MAP workbook and attached a short eval-plan-brief.md that summarizes the canary and go/no-go criteria for MAP milestone 2. Summary of agreed items: 

- Token assumptions (finalized for pilot): Search=100 tokens/req, Rerank=740 tokens/req, Summary=1,900 tokens/req
- Batching assumptions: interactive factor 1.5; batch factor 8
- Cache hit modeling: search 25%, rerank 10%, summaries 0%
- Canary runbook: 10k requests/day (3 days), metrics: total tokens, cost per 1M tokens, 95p latency, quality regression on eval prompts.
- Next: procurement requested a MAP redline PDF; Ben please help coordinate legal redlines (attached). Also sending a DocuSign invite for the MAP (priors + eval acceptance) once procurement confirms internal PO/approval window.

Link to workbook + eval prompts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-eval-plan (see document 'eval-plan-brief.md').

Tom — can you confirm procurement’s preferred timeline for signature? If we can get sign-off by EOD Wed (2/23) we’ll schedule the canary for the week of 2/28 and aim to deliver the tokens/$ sensitivity report within 72 hours of canary completion.

Attachments: eval-plan-brief.md, redlines-MAP-v1.pdf
